title: Protocol for BATTLE-1EX: A High-Resolution Imaging Method to Visualize Whole Synaptic Structures and their Components in the Nervous System
protocol: Perform stereotaxic injection of viruses according to Kohara et al. (2014) and Kohara et al. (2020).
Prepare surgery set up in the safety cabinet in P2 biosafety room.
Place the stereotaxic injection systems on the safety cabinet.
Prepare the surgery tools, suture needle with thread, and microdrill on the safety cabinet.
Prepare skin marker, cotton swabs, and ointment pot added with commercial chlorine disinfecting cleaner (Hypochlorous acid >0.1%).
Prepare pipette man (P2, P20, P200) and filtered tips on the safety cabinet.
Put 50 ml autoclaved PBS and isodine.
Place the anesthetic machine for isoflurane beside the safety cabinet and fill with isoflurane.
Connect the tube between anesthetic machine and gasmask attached in stereotaxic injection system.
Connect the tube between the extra isoflurane retrieve bottle and the gas mask attached in stereotaxic injection system.
Place a small desk stand with a magnifying glass on the safety cabinet.
Prepare small square parafilms (about 1 cm × 1 cm) for back-filling sharp glass pipette with virus solution.
Place a small shaver on the side desk for cutting the skull hair of the mouse.
Prepare Hamilton syringe and sharp glass pipettes on the desk in P2 biosafety room.
Place a 50-mL centrifuge tube filled with mineral oil in the tube stand on the desk.
Prepare Hamilton syringe, sharp glass pipette box, and backfill syringe with sharp tube.
Remove metal joint fitting of Hamilton syringe and place it on the desk.
Fill metal joint fitting with mineral oil on the desk.
Fill mineral oil on the upper lid of 50-mL centrifuge tube on the desk.
Insert the tip of Hamilton syringe without metal joint fitting (but with plastic compression fitting) into the upper lid of 50-mL centrifuge tube filled with mineral oil.
Fill mineral oil in the Hamilton syringe and remove air in the Hamilton syringe by repeating plunger pushing and withdrawing.
After removing the bubble air in the Hamilton syringe, connect the Hamilton syringe with metal joint fitting (avoid trapping any air).
Backfill sharp glass pipette with mineral oil by using backfill syringe with sharp tube (avoid trapping any air bubbles in the sharp glass pipette).
Connect a sharp glass pipette filled with mineral oil to a Hamilton syringe also filled with mineral oil.
Attach the Hamilton syringe connected with the sharp glass pipette to the stereotaxic injector in the safety cabinet.
Position the attached Hamilton syringe at the highest point just above the mouse head.
Anesthetize an older than 8-week-old mouse in a box filled with 3% isoflurane.
Shave the skull hair of the anesthetized mouse using a slim hair cutter.
Fix the mouse head with ear bars in the stereotaxic injection system.
Insert the fixed left ear bar into the left ear canal of the mouse.
Adjust the mouse's head direction to be parallel to the ground.
Insert the right ear bar around the right ear canal of the mouse.
Fix the right ear bar when it is adequately inserted into the mouse's right ear canal.
Confirm that the mouse head can rotate vertically to the fixed ear bar.
Fit a gas anesthesia mask to the mouse nose.
Adjust the z-position of the gas anesthesia mask at roughly the correct position.
Apply eye ointment by cotton swabs on the mouse eyes to prevent dry eyes.
Sanitize the mouse head hair with povidone iodine and cotton swabs.
Cover the mouse body with a trimmed surgical paper.
Make an incision on the mouse head skin to expose skull bone using small surgical clamps.
Wipe jelly on the exposed skull bone by cotton swab.
Mark points at Bregma and Lambda using a skin marker.
Move and lower a sharp glass pipette to just above the Lambda point.
Contact the tip of the sharp glass pipette with the surface of the skull at the Lambda point.
Monitor the tip through magnifying stand glass (×5).
Record the dorso-ventral (DV) position of the Lambda point by reading the scale of the stereotaxic injection system.
Move and lower the sharp glass pipette to the Bregma point.
Contact the tip of the sharp glass pipette with the surface of the skull at the Bregma point.
Monitor the tip through magnifying stand glass (×5).
Record the DV position of the Bregma point by reading the scale of the stereotaxic injection system.
Adjust the position of the gas anesthesia mask if necessary.
Confirm that DV position of Bregma equals that of Lambda and record AP and ML positions of Bregma.
Move the sharp glass pipette to the predetermined injection site.
Mark the injection site using skin marker.
Drill slowly at the marked injection site using a microdrill.
Carefully make a hole when the skull bone becomes thin, using the bent tip of the needle.
Dig up small bones at the injection site with the bent tip of the needle.
Remove blood from the area using cotton swabs and apply sterilized PBS.
Place a small piece of parafilm on the ear bar.
Apply 2 μL of mixed lentiviruses onto the parafilm.
Lower the sharp glass pipette into the water drop of mixed lentiviruses.
Suck up 1.2–1.5 μL of mixed lentiviruses into the pipette at a speed of 90 nL/s.
Move the sharp glass pipette to the injection site and lower it to a position 0.3 mm deeper than the injection site.
Return to the injection site after lowering the pipette (to create space).
Inject 1 μL of mixed lentiviruses solution at a speed of 30 nL/s.
Wait for 5 minutes before removing the sharp glass pipette from the injection site to avoid spreading lentivirus along the needle track.
Stitch skin of mouse head.
Place the mouse in a new cage and heat the cage by the heater sheet until the mouse becomes awake.
Wait for 3 weeks until the second AAV injection.
Prepare surgery set up in the safety cabinet in P2 biosafety room three weeks after the first injection.
Make the injection hole by a vent needle.
Inject 1 μL of mixed AAV solution into the same injection site as the first one at a speed of 30 nL/s.
Wait for 5 min.
Inject 1 μL of mixed AAV solution into the same injection again at a speed of 30 nL/s.
Use hypochlorous acid (>0.1%) to sterilize the used tip for AAV.
Anesthetize mice with an intraperitoneal administration of a mixed anesthetic (medetomidine, midazolam, and butorphanol).
Perfuse transcardially with ice-cold 4% PFA in PBS using a peristaltic pump.
Postfix removed brain in the same solution for 24 hours.
Transfer fixed brain to 30% sucrose in PBS.
Embed brain in optimal cutting temperature compound.
Freeze brain with isopentane and liquid nitrogen.
Section brain sagittally at 60 μm thickness using a cryostat (Leica).
Transfer sections into PBS and place them in a 12-well plate.
Roughly check the fluorescence of the sections through an inverted microscope to select sections for Expansion microscopy (ExM).
Cover parafilm on the empty chip tray.
Press a magnetic stirrer bar on parafilm to create wells for immunostaining.
Use a paintbrush to transfer sections between the wells.
Incubate freely floating sections in citrate buffer at 80°C for 30 minutes in a 1.5 ml tube.
Allow the sections to cool slowly to room temperature (22°C-26°C).
Wash the sections five times with PBS for 5 minutes each.
Trim sections roughly using Iris scissors before immunostaining to save reagent.
Incubate sections in blocking buffer in a parafilm well plate for 1 hour at room temperature (22°C–26°C) with shaking.

Incubate sections with primary chicken polyclonal antibody to GFP (1:500), rat monoclonal antibody to RFP (1:100), mouse monoclonal antibody to Bassoon (1:100), and rabbit polyclonal antibody to Homer1 (1:100) in blocking buffer for 2 days (44 hours–52 hours) at 4°C, followed by washing four times with blocking buffer, each time for 5 minutes with shaking.

Incubate sections with secondary anti-chicken donkey antibody conjugated with Alexa488 dye (1:200), anti-rat donkey antibody conjugated with Alexa568 dye (1:100), anti-mouse goat antibody conjugated with Atto647N dye (1:100), and anti-rabbit goat antibody conjugated with CF405M dye (1:100) in blocking buffer for 24 hours at 4°C with shaking.
Wash sections three times with blocking buffer, three times with high salt PBS, and three times with PBS, each time for 5 minutes with shaking.
Incubate sections with Acryloyl-X in PBS for more than 6 hours at room temperature without shaking.
Wash sections three times with PBS, each time for 5 minutes.
Remove PBS from sections by washing once with reagent before gelling.
Mix monomer solution, 4-hydroxy-TEMPO, APS, and TEMED just before use to prepare the gelling solution.
Keep the prepared gelling solution at 4°C until use.
Cut coverslips using a glass cutter for spacer placement on the glass slide.
Place two cut coverslips as spacers on the glass slide.
Drop 50 μL of gelling solution onto the glass slide.
Transfer sections into the gelling solution using a paintbrush.
Sandwich the sections between the glass slide and top coverslip.
Incubate the sandwiched sections for 2 hours at 37°C.
Trim hippocampus regions minimally from gelled sections with a razor blade under a stereo microscope (Leica S9i).
Drop digestion buffer on the sample and peel off gently from the edge.
Immerse sections in 500 μL of digestion buffer at room temperature (22°C–26°C) for 12 h.
Wash three times with PBS for 5 min.
Transfer gels into a new container that is large enough to accommodate expanded gels.
Wash samples three times with water for 15 min to reach the final expansion size.
Put expanded gel on the coverslip.
Put silicon sheet surrounding the gel.
Put silicon sheet on the sample.
Transfer samples on coverslip with paintbrush.
Remove extra buffer by Kimwipes.
Pause the procedure after imaging.
Store samples in PBS at 4°C in the dark.
